subject: Integration kickoff — dedicated capacity constraints, queues, and reranker plan
messages:
From: Elliot Harper <elliot@monetapay.com>
To: connor_obrien <connor@redwood.example>, marissa_cole <marissa@redwood.example>
Cc: Rina Sato <rina@monetapay.com>, MonetaPay Infra <infra@monetapay.com>
Date: Mon, 20 Jul 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Follow-up + prioritization after today's demo

Thanks again for the demo today — that was very helpful. A quick recap from our side and a proposal for next steps so we can lock sizing and procurement timelines:

- Primary goal: move embeddings + reranker workload to Dedicated capacity for predictable latency during checkouts (peak windows 09:00-11:00 and 17:00-19:00 PST).
- Current traffic: ~350 inference requests/minute (chat + 3 embeddings calls per checkout) with median prompt lengths ~220 tokens, reranker uses 8 candidates per request.
- Soft SLO: p95 generation latency <= 180ms; hard requirement for checkout flows is p99 < 500ms.
- Questions we need answered from Redwood before procurement:
  1) Auth model for Private/Dedicated (SAML + service principal) and sample token flow for our edge service.
  2) Queueing behavior under burst (what queue depth per worker / backpressure semantics).
  3) Autoscaling windows: min capacity, warm-up time for GPU pools, and whether we can reserve capacity for peak hours.
  4) Embeddings throughput: recommended batch sizing and expected tokens/sec for the model you proposed.

Attached: a rough sketch of our request flow and an example of the auth flow we currently use internally. Please call out any blockers for our procurement timeline (we're targeting contract sign-off by 2026-08-10).

Thanks,
Elliot
Elliot Harper
Head of Product Engineering, MonetaPay
[Attachment: 20260720-kickoff-ops-diagram.pdf (diagram, 1.2MB)]

From: connor_obrien <connor@redwood.example>
To: Elliot Harper <elliot@monetapay.com>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa@redwood.example>, karthik_iyer <karthik@redwood.example>
Date: Mon, 20 Jul 2026 17:01:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Follow-up + prioritization after today's demo

Thanks Elliot — good notes. Short answers up front, longer follow-up below.

Quick answers:
- Auth: we support OIDC service accounts for Dedicated and can integrate with your SAML IdP for admin console access. I'll attach a sample service-principal flow.
- Queues/backpressure: Redwood's worker runtime exposes a bounded in-memory request queue per GPU with configurable backpressure and non-blocking rejection options; default queue depth is 1024 requests per worker but can be tuned.
- Autoscale: warm-up for a cold GPU (scheduling + container spin) is ~90-120s; we recommend reserved baseline capacity for peak windows and short burst autoscaling for +50% capacity.
- Embeddings: recommended batch size 64 for your median sequence length; expected steady-state throughput ~1.1k embeddings/sec per A100-equivalent GPU (model/quantization dependent).

I pulled in Marissa and Karthik to map a concrete sizing proposal and a couple of engineering artifacts:
- marissa: will share a deployment/queueing diagram and a proposed baseline capacity plan.
- karthik: will confirm limits for concurrent reranker jobs and any recommended client-side throttling.

Next steps we propose:
1) Redwood -> share sample auth config (service principal) and the kickoff ops diagram (we will attach sample-auth-config.json).
2) MonetaPay -> confirm peak window calendar and an hourly traffic dump (CSV) for two recent weekdays.
3) Technical sync: 45 minutes with infra + backend SDK owners (we can do Wed or Thu this week).

I'll follow up with the attachments and a proposed meeting time.

—Connor
Connor O'Brien
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: sample-auth-config.json (text)]

From: marissa_cole <marissa@redwood.example>
To: Elliot Harper <elliot@monetapay.com>, connor_obrien <connor@redwood.example>, karthik_iyer <karthik@redwood.example>
Cc: neha_kapoor <neha@redwood.example>
Date: Tue, 21 Jul 2026 09:38:00 -0700
Subject: Proposed Dedicated baseline + queueing pattern (details)

On Mon, 20 Jul 2026 at 5:01 PM connor_obrien <connor@redwood.example> wrote:
> Thanks Elliot — good notes. Short answers up front, longer follow-up below.
>
> Quick answers:
> - Auth: we support OIDC service accounts for Dedicated and can integrate with your SAML IdP for admin console access. I'll attach a sample service-principal flow.

Thanks — below is a proposed baseline that maps to your traffic profile and p95 latency target. This is a starting point we can refine after we receive your hourly traffic dump.

Baseline proposal (initial):
- Model choices: 1x generation model for chat (gptx-redwood-2-medium) + 1x embedding model (embed-redwood-1). Reranker uses the generation model in rerank-only mode (no streaming).
- Capacity: Reserve 3 GPUs (A100-equivalent) as baseline in Dedicated for steady-state. Autoscale policy: add 2 GPUs when queue depth > 600 for 30s, add additional 2 GPUs if queue depth > 1000 for 60s. Max cap 8 GPUs for initial rollout.
- Concurrency: Set per-GPU concurrency to 16 gen requests and 48 embedding requests (embeddings are cheaper per token). We recommend isolating reranker requests on a dedicated logical queue to avoid head-of-line blocking.
- Queues: three logical queues per deployment: realtime-chat, embeddings, rerankers. Queue depth caps: 1024 / 2048 / 512 respectively. For each queue we support FIFO with priority bump for checkout requests (you can tag traffic).
- Client-side behavior: implement token-bucket throttling at your checkout proxy (burst=200 requests, refill=50 req/s) and exponential backoff on 429s starting at 50ms.
- Warm pools: we can schedule warm standby GPUs that are provisioned but not accepting requests (reduces warm-up to ~20s at added cost).

Observability / SLOs:
- We will expose per-queue p50/p95/p99 timesteps, per-token cost, and per-route rejection metrics in the Redwood Console.

Attachments: ops diagram (shows queueing + warm pools) and sample-auth-config.json for your infra team.

Open questions for MonetaPay:
1) Can you confirm maximum concurrent checkout flows you expect during the 09:00-11:00 peak?
2) Will reranker requests be initiated within the same HTTP request path as checkout (synchronous), or can they be decoupled to an async path?
3) Any internal compliance requirements for ephemeral key rotation (we support 24h - 7d rotation windows)?

If those answers look right I recommend we move to a short POC for the checkout path with the baseline above — 2 weeks of metrics collection to validate queueing thresholds and autoscale triggers.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: 20260720-kickoff-ops-diagram.pdf (PDF)]

From: karthik_iyer <karthik@redwood.example>
To: Elliot Harper <elliot@monetapay.com>, marissa_cole <marissa@redwood.example>, connor_obrien <connor@redwood.example>
Cc: neha_kapoor <neha@redwood.example>
Date: Fri, 23 Jul 2026 09:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Proposed Dedicated baseline + queueing pattern (confirming concurrency & next steps)

Thanks all — quick confirmation from infra/runtime side.

- Concurrency limits above look good; one clarification: the 16 gen concurrency per GPU assumes batching; if your traffic is highly bursty with short prompts we may see lower batch efficiency and should compensate by raising concurrency or adding GPUs.
- Reranker isolation: we strongly prefer decoupling rerankers to an async path if your checkout can accept 50-150ms extra latency for eventual ranking; otherwise we will reserve a small hot pool (1 GPU) dedicated to rerank only.
- Autoscale tuning: the queue-depth triggers Marissa proposed are safe. We will also provide a sliding-average CPU/GPU util trigger as a secondary signal.

Next steps (action owners):
- MonetaPay: provide hourly CSV for two weekdays and confirm whether rerankers must be sync (Elliot).
- Connor: schedule the 45-minute technical sync and drop calendar invite (Connor).
- Marissa: prepare POC runbook and metrics dashboard template; will upload to the Drive link above (Marissa).
- Karthik: will prepare a short note on batching expectations and a formula to translate batch size -> tokens/sec per GPU.

I'll aim to have the batching note by EOD Monday. If MonetaPay confirms sync availability we'll lock a slot.

—Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Infra Architect, Redwood Inference
